item.title: China, Indonesia Agree on Closer Defense Ties in High-Level Talks in Jakarta
item.description: China and Indonesia agreed to deepen their military, maritime and technology cooperation in high-level talks in Jakarta on Friday, underscoring Beijing’s growing regional reach at a time of renewed uncertainty over US security commitments in Asia.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara

item.title: Our Town Chapter 3: One Little Bacon-Wrapped Sausage (Podcast)
item.description: Backers of the venture are big fans of a town in Idaho where a preacher with a flamethrower tells our reporters how much he hates feminism.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Beemsterboer

item.title: Analysis of Germany's Economic Challenges, Regional Elections
item.description: The German economy is facing a squeeze on many sides: higher energy prices, tariffs from the US, increased competition from China. Meanwhile, the far-right Alternative for Germany party is expected to make major gains in upcoming regional elections. Bloomberg's Christoph Rauwald and Michael Nienaber report. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hamid Karzai on Life Under the Taliban
item.description: Former Afghanistan president Hamid Karzai talks to Mishal Husain about regime-change wars, conflict with Pakistan and why he's still talking to the Taliban. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Karzai Says Education of Women Is Key to Afghanistan's Future
item.description: Afghanistan's former president Hamid Karzai said he continues to urge Taliban officials to allow girls and women to return to education and work — a key obstacle to the group gaining international legitimacy. He made the comments during an interview on The Mishal Husain Show. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Swiss Voters Are Set to Reject Stricter Neutrality, Poll Shows
item.description: A plebiscite on making Switzerland’s traditional neutrality stricter is likely to be rejected by the country’s voters, according to a poll ahead of the Sept. 27 ballot measure.
item.dc:creator: Bastian Benrath-Wright

item.title: Oil-Rich Kazakhstan Set For Elections as Tokayev Bolsters Power
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to hold elections for a new single-chamber parliament as President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev continues a political shake-up that leaves open the prospect of extending his rule in Central Asia’s largest energy producer.
item.dc:creator: Nariman Gizitdinov

item.title: Hong Kong Convicts Tiananmen Vigil Leaders of Subversion
item.description: A Hong Kong court convicted two former organizers of the city’s annual Tiananmen Square vigils of inciting subversion, in a closely watched test of the national security law imposed by Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Alan Wong

item.title: MAGA Inc.’s War Chest Climbs to $404 Million After Zero Spending
item.description: President Donald Trump’s super PAC war chest grew to nearly $404 million after getting $3 million in donations and interest payments in July, but it spent nothing that month to boost the prospects of Republican candidates in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Bill Allison

item.title: US Accuses China of Wrongful Detention of American Scholar
item.description: China is wrongfully detaining American scholar U Min Zin, the US State Department said, making the case a priority for the Trump administration as the countries’ leaders prepare to meet in Washington next month.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Nancy Kissinger, a Force Beside Her Diplomat Husband, Dead at 92
item.description: Nancy Kissinger, who transformed from a foreign policy specialist into a force beside her diplomat husband, Henry, and helped cement their place among New York’s social elite, has died. She was 92.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Gordon

item.title: Russia Holds Rare Missile Test Near Islands Claimed by Japan
item.description: Russia conducted a rare missile exercise involving naval vessels and a land-based launcher near islands in its Far East that are also claimed by Japan, adding to recent friction between the two nations.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Gale

item.title: Kim’s Sister Mocks South Korea as US ‘Puppet’ Over Drill Cutback
item.description: North Korea mocked South Korea for being a US “puppet” after President Donald Trump unilaterally curtailed the two countries’ joint military drills.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Imran Khan Moved to Hospital Following Pakistan Court Order
item.description: Pakistan’s former prime minister, Imran Khan, has been transferred to a hospital from prison after an order from the country’s top court, according to his Tehreek-e-Insaf party.
item.dc:creator: Tooba Khan

item.title: Trump Threatens ‘Economic D-Day’ Against Iran | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/20/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Republican Rep. Mike Lawler of New York says the US should "hold the Chinese to account" for facilitating Iran's illicit oil trade as President Donald Trump pushes an economic "D-Day" against Tehran. Josh Lipsky, Vice President & Chair of International Economics at the Atlantic Council, says Beijing is betting President Donald Trump wants to make a "big show" of economic pressure on Iran but will stop short of squeezing Chinese banks. Dana Stroul, Senior Fellow and Director of Research at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, says imposing more punishing economic pressure on Iran will depend on cooperation from partners including the UAE and China. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stroul: Trump's Iran Economic Push Needs Partners
item.description: Dana Stroul, Senior Fellow and Director of Research at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, says imposing more punishing economic pressure on Iran will depend on cooperation from partners including the UAE and China. She says the UAE's move to cut economic ties with Tehran could be "extremely significant" if fully implemented, while warning China has tools to retaliate against additional US pressure. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Risks China Blowback With Plan to Choke Iran’s Economy
item.description: When Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent vowed to ramp up pressure on Iran by targeting its economic partners, he echoed former President George W. Bush’s warning to US allies after the Sept. 11 attacks.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin and Magdalena Del Valle

item.title: US Sanctions Fishing Fleet Accused of Shipping Cocaine to Mexico
item.description: The US Treasury sanctioned a fleet of fishing vessels suspected of smuggling tons of cocaine to Mexico each month, ultimately bound for the US.
item.dc:creator: Maya Averbuch

item.title: Lipsky: China Could Limit Trump's Iran Pressure
item.description: Josh Lipsky, Vice President of International Economics at the Atlantic Council, says Beijing is betting President Donald Trump wants to make a "big show" of economic pressure on Iran but will stop short of squeezing Chinese banks. Lipsky also says the US is testing investors' patience in a way it hasn't for a long time as debt tops $40 trillion. Lipsky also weighs in on ongoing US-Canada tariff negotiations. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, Japan, South Korea Urge North Korea to Halt ‘Provocations’
item.description: The US, Japan and South Korea held a three-way call to coordinate their response to North Korea’s barrage of short-range ballistic missiles, after Pyongyang dismissed President Donald Trump’s overtures to revive dialogue with leader Kim Jong Un.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi and Sarah Hilton
